newsitem.title: USA: W. House reaching out to Congress--budget official.
newsitem.headline: W. House reaching out to Congress--budget official.

text.p: A White House official on Friday played down the significance of the recent war of words over the budget and said the administration was reaching out to Republican lawmakers to try to reach an agreement.
"The budget process by definition is a bit messy," Lawrence Haas, Associate Director of the Office of Management and Budget, told Reuters Financial Television.
"We are going to continue to reach out .... We want to negotiate right now," he added.

The war of words over the budget outlook escalated on Thursday as the Republican chairman of the Senate Budget Committee said he felt chances of negotiating an agreement with the White House were finished.

Haas though argued that undue optimism or pessimism about the budget outlook is usually unwarranted and suggested that the administration was still trying to make progress behind the scenes in hammering out a balanced budget deal.
"We continue to believe that we are going to get it done this year," he said.
Haas doubted that the budget talks would hit a snag because President Clinton's knee injury would remove him from the process.
"I really don't think this is a major impediment," he said. "He's (Clinton's) a very energetic guy. I don't think it's going to slow him down."
Haas also played down fears that the recent public bickering over the budget was a harbinger of a breakdown in talks and an eventual government shutdown.
"It's hard for us to believe that anyone wants to go through that again," he said, referring to the government shutdowns in late 1995 and early 1996.
Echoing comments by other administration officials, Haas said that the White House was not prepared to put forward another budget proposal, as demanded by Republican lawmakers.
But he made clear that administration was willing to alter its original proposal in the course of negotiations with Congress.
